item.text: {"question_id":"6B.7","answer":"During 2023, formal rules contained some anti-arbitrariness safeguards: disability law provided eligibility-linked social assistance, complaint, investigation, litigation, and legal-aid routes; Shanghai specified categories, payment deadlines, and controlled or direct bank-account payment for a temporary subsidy; and Deqin reported monthly eligibility checks and financial-information verification. These materials establish formal design and selected administrative practice, but not accessibility, reversal rates, independent adjudication, or protection against political retaliation. The revised Administrative Reconsideration Law was enacted in 2023 but took effect only on 1 January 2024, so it cannot demonstrate practical protection during the target period. Contrary evidence shows that political control could condition opportunities and rights: authorities used censorship, account restrictions, religious controls, detention, and employment or business pressure against criticism, religious activity, or politically disfavored conduct; a Zhejiang study found politically connected firms received higher corporate social-credit scores; and judicial institutions remained structurally dependent on party-state bodies. The evidence therefore supports limited procedural and payment safeguards in ordinary welfare administration, but not a finding that welfare, permits, jobs, food, or housing were insulated from political loyalty or punishment. Direct evidence tying political retaliation specifically to each core welfare benefit is incomplete, and some adverse evidence concerns broader rights, business, or judicial systems rather than welfare allocation itself.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0020-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0019-E002","BATCH-0008-E005","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0010-E019","BATCH-0010-E024","BATCH-0010-E028","BATCH-0021-E016","BATCH-0017-E012","BATCH-0003-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal disability-law remedies and local welfare procedures do not establish practical accessibility, independence, reversal rates, or politically sensitive case outcomes.","Shanghai and Deqin are local examples and cannot establish national administrative practice.","The revised Administrative Reconsideration Law was not effective during 2023.","Evidence of political punishment is stronger for speech, religion, association, courts, and business activity than for direct denial of welfare, permits, food, or housing.","The Zhejiang social-credit study is local and its observation-year fit to 2023 is uncertain; several institutional findings are system-level rather than personally attributable to Xi."],"corrections_made":["Reduced the positive weight assigned to formal rules, local monitoring, and payment channels because implementation and remedy effectiveness were not demonstrated.","Removed the implication that complaint, mediation, litigation, legal aid, or supervision constituted effective protection for politically sensitive applicants.","Added the concrete political-allocation and opportunity evidence identified by the critique while preserving its scope and attribution limits.","Corrected the temporal treatment of the Administrative Reconsideration Law by noting that it was enacted in 2023 but effective in 2024."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Direct evidence is still needed on whether political loyalty or dissent affected eligibility, permits, jobs, food, or housing decisions during 2023.","A fuller review should seek appeal accessibility, reversal, enforcement, and distribution data, including politically sensitive cases and subnational variation."]}
